text.p: Shareholders of Metway Bank Ltd, the only listed entity in the Queensland government's plan to create a state "mega bank", unaminously approved the merger on Wednesday.
The government proposes to merge Metway with Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) and Suncorp Insurance and Finance, both of which are owned by the government.
Under the multi-faceted deal, Metway shareholders are being offered the choice of either holding on to their shares or accepting A$4.80 a share plus a four cent dividend.
The government owns 10.28 percent of Metway.
Independent experts Grant Samuel has estimated the merged group would have a market capitalisation of A$2.2 billion.
The government holding would be between 71 percent and 100 percent depending on the number of shareholders who elect to receive cash rather than retain their shares.
The government has said it intends to reduce its shareholding to less than 15 percent within five years.
Metway shares were at A$5.65 at 12.10 p.m. (0110 GMT) on Wednesday, up a cent.
